variants.prompt: A logistics warehouse uses $36$ meters of steel safety barrier to enclose a three-sided rectangular staging zone against an existing $18$-meter interior bulkhead wall (so the side along the bulkhead can be at most $18$ meters long). Treating the staging area as a function of the side $w$ perpendicular to the bulkhead, what depth $w$ (in meters) gives an enclosed area of $160$ square meters?

steps.explain: Express the side along the bulkhead in terms of w from the three-sided barrier length.
Write the enclosed staging area as a single-variable function of w.
Set the area function equal to the required area.
Rearrange into standard form and divide by 2.
Factor the quadratic equation.
Check l = 36 - 2w: w = 8 gives l = 20 > 18 (exceeds the bulkhead), whereas w = 10 gives l = 16 <= 18.

contextCheck.note: Three-sided warehouse barrier and bulkhead wall limit follow real rectangle perimeter/area laws with consistent meter and square-meter units.

blindSolve.edgeRejected: w = 8 (requires bulkhead side l = 20 m, exceeding the 18 m bulkhead limit)
